title: Finding a way back
hook: A route can be summarized by a displacement.

knows: Animals can respond to cues and conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy map, a forager goes 3 steps north and 4 steps east from its nest. Which direct direction points back to the nest?

misconception: The stated evidence implies a different interpretation or a universal conclusion.
objective: In a toy map, a forager goes 3 steps north and 4 steps east from its nest. Which direct direction points back to the nest?

claims.text: In a toy map, a forager goes 3 steps north and 4 steps east from its nest. Which direct direction points back to the nest? The outward route ends north and east of the nest. The return arrow points southwest, undoing the net displacement. This is a toy map of path integration, not evidence that a particular animal uses these exact distances.
claims.source: Unverified research lead; confirm exact claim and species with an independent source reviewer: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology ; where applicable consult a specialist source. The illustrated observations and values are stipulated toy examples.

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative model and do not depict observed data.
On a toy map a nest lies west and south of a forager. Which direction leads directly home? West and south combine to give a southwest direction.
